TX-2025892-HB1.s: This law changes rules for youth camps in Texas. It requires camp emergency plans, safety training, weather alerts, backup internet, and some notice to parents and local officials. It also sets rules for inspections and can lead to license denial or suspension if a camp does not follow the new requirements.

TX-2025892-HB16.s: The law changes how parts of Texas courts work, including court duties, clerk jobs, record rules, and some case priorities. It creates or changes several judicial districts and district courts in counties such as Fort Bend, Harris, Montgomery, Brazoria, Rockwall, Ellis, Comal, and others, and it also changes some district attorney offices. Some parts take effect on dates from December 1, 2025, through January 1, 2029, and the law also allows some fees and raises one criminal penalty.

TX-2025892-HB18.s: The law limits certain campaign donations and spending for lawmakers and some political committees during a member’s unexcused absence from a legislative session. It bars accepting donations above a set daily amount and spending on travel, food, or lodging tied to that absence, and it can lead to a civil penalty of up to $5,000 for each violation. It takes effect 91 days after the last day of the legislative session and applies to covered donations or spending on or after that date.

TX-2025892-HB192.s: The law applies to counties with more than 3.3 million people and limits when they can cut or move money from law enforcement budgets. It requires voter approval before a county can reduce or shift certain sheriff or constable funding, lets residents file a complaint if a county does this without approval, and gives the comptroller a role in checking it. If a county does not get the needed approval, it can face limits on its tax rate until the money is restored or voters approve the change. It took effect on the 91st day after the legislative session ended.

TX-2025892-HB20.s: The law creates a state program for local governments to name a nonprofit or financial institution that can take disaster relief donations during a declared disaster, and it also requires local websites to share that information and tips on avoiding scams. It creates new crimes for dishonest disaster fundraising and for taking disaster-related property, and it raises the punishment in some cases. It also lets donors or donees sue for 300% of the money taken, plus lawyer fees, and it takes effect 91 days after the legislative session ends.

TX-2025892-HB22.s: The bill would let the comptroller use a state fund to help pay for early warning systems and other emergency communication gear, including equipment, operations, and admin costs. It would also let the Broadband Development Office give contracts, grants, low-interest loans, and other help for these systems and for interoperable emergency communication equipment and infrastructure. The act would take effect on the 91st day after the last day of the legislative session.

TX-2025892-HB23.s: The bill would exempt certain nonprofit-owned land and buildings from property tax in counties with 3.3 million people or more if the property is used to promote agriculture, support youth, and provide educational help in the community. It applies to nonprofits organized for charitable, educational, and scientific purposes. The law takes effect on January 1, 2026.

TX-2025892-HB25.s: The bill lets pharmacists give out ivermectin without a prescription if they follow state pharmacy board rules and any needed instructions for proper use. It also gives pharmacists protection from civil, criminal, and professional discipline when they act reasonably and follow the law. The Texas State Board of Pharmacy may adopt rules to carry it out. It takes effect on the 91st day after the last day of the legislative session.

TX-2025892-HB26.s: The law lets sheriffs and constables in counties with more than 3.3 million people make contracts to provide law enforcement services for local governments, property owners' groups, or landowners. The county government could not block or change those contracts, and the sheriff or constable would set the terms. It was signed by the governor and takes effect on the 91st day after the last day of the legislative session.

TX-2025892-HB4.s: This law redraws the Texas districts used to elect members of the U.S. House of Representatives. It sets out new district lines for those elections and says one member is elected from each district. It affects Texas voters and the counties and census areas listed in the law. It took effect on September 5, 2025.

TX-2025892-HB8.s: Texas HB 8 would change how public school tests are given and used for school accountability. It would move the state from STAAR to a new assessment program by the 2027-2028 school year, and it would require schools to give parents access to test results and notices through online portals. The bill would also change some test subjects, special education testing rules, and limits on using common core standards in state tests.

TX-2025892-HCR13.s: The resolution urges the federal government to act to stop the spread of New World screwworm in Texas. It asks federal agencies and Congress to speed up a control facility, work with Mexico, approve treatments and pesticides, and support research with Texas A&M AgriLife. It is aimed at protecting Texas ranchers, livestock, pets, wildlife, and people from a parasite that can kill animals and harm the state economy.

TX-2025892-HCR14.s: This resolution congratulates Lori Rickert on her retirement as presiding judge for Brazoria County Court at Law No. 4 and Probate Court. It also notes her long service in that role and her work on a range of court cases and the county's Recovery Court program.

TX-2025892-HCR2.s: This resolution asks the Texas Legislature to honor the victims of the July 2025 Hill Country floods and express condolences to their families, friends, and neighbors. It is a formal statement of sympathy about the disaster and the people affected by it.

TX-2025892-HCR20.s: This resolution commemorates the 75th anniversary of St. Ann's Catholic School in Midland and offers best wishes to the school and its people. It also calls for an official copy of the resolution to be prepared for the school as a sign of respect from the Texas House and Senate.

TX-2025892-HCR3.s: This resolution commemorates the dedication of Children's Emergency Relief International’s new Austin headquarters, which was named for former Texas state representative George M. Cowden. It also recognizes Cowden’s service in Texas government and his other public roles. The measure was adopted by both chambers and signed by the governor.

TX-2025892-HCR4.s: The resolution congratulates Rickey and Anne Lowe of Horseshoe Bay on their 47th wedding anniversary. It also asks that an official copy be prepared for them as a sign of respect from the Texas House and Senate. It was signed by the governor.

TX-2025892-HR128.s: The resolution would change Texas House rules on leave of absence and penalties for members who miss sessions without leave to block House action. It adds or updates penalties such as fines, payment of sergeant-at-arms costs, reprimand, censure, loss of chair or vice-chair roles, and possible expulsion. It also sets rules for how these penalties would be paid, how budgets and seniority could be reduced, and how the House Administration Committee would handle notices and reports.

TX-2025892-SB1.s: The law adds safety rules for campgrounds and youth camps in Texas, especially for places near flood areas. It requires campground cabins in floodplains to have roof access ladders and evacuation plans, and it bars or limits licenses for youth camps with cabins in floodplains. It also requires youth camps to keep emergency plans, train staff and campers, post evacuation routes, keep backup internet and weather alert systems, and share approved plans with parents and local emergency managers.

TX-2025892-SB11.s: The bill creates a legal defense for some people prosecuted in Texas who were victims of human trafficking or forced prostitution. It would apply when force, fraud, or coercion led them to do the act, and the person must meet set conditions to use the defense. It takes effect 91 days after the last day of the legislative session and applies only to offenses committed on or after that date.

TX-2025892-SB12.s: The bill gives the Texas attorney general the power to prosecute crimes under state election laws and to represent the state in those cases. It also requires law enforcement and local prosecutors to share reports and other information about those cases with the attorney general. The law applies only to offenses committed on or after its effective date, which is the 91st day after the last day of the legislative session.

TX-2025892-SB14.s: Local governments would have to give builders and developers credits against water and wastewater impact fees for certain projects that save, reuse, or reduce water use. The bill covers eligible facilities, systems, or products that cut water demand, lower wastewater needs, reduce stormwater needs, or meet stronger water-saving standards. Local governments would also have to set fair rules for figuring out and approving the credits. It takes effect January 1, 2026.

TX-2025892-SB16.s: The bill became law and adds new crimes for real property theft and real property fraud, which cover certain theft or fraud tied to land or buildings. It also sets recording rules for some court papers and county records, and it requires restitution, or repayment, for people, title companies, or insurers harmed by these offenses. The law also directs county clerks to send notice to law enforcement if someone says a real estate filing after January 1, 2026, is fraudulent, and it adds steps for inmate-filed liens that may be fake.

TX-2025892-SB18.s: The bill would let certain local water districts or authorities build and keep some small dams or reservoirs without getting a permit from the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality, if they are used for erosion, floodwater, and sediment control. It would apply to projects on land they own or control, and to small water storage of no more than 200 acre-feet. The bill was vetoed by the Governor.

TX-2025892-SB3.s: The bill creates a state grant program to help cities, counties, and other local governments pay to install outdoor warning sirens in flash flood-prone areas. It also requires local governments in those areas to install, maintain, test, and operate sirens when the state board says they are needed, unless a working siren already meets state guidance. The law took effect immediately.

TX-2025892-SB5.s: The bill gives $200 million from the state savings fund to the governor’s disaster programs for federal matching money and other disaster response and recovery needs. It also gives $50 million for local flood warning sirens and gauges in listed counties, and $28 million for grants to improve weather forecasting and flood warnings. If another camp safety bill passes, it also sets aside money for the health department to carry out that law and lets it raise license fees to cover the cost. It took effect immediately.

TX-2025892-SB54.s: The law changes how voters can be accepted when their home address is no longer current because they moved within the same county. It also says some voter registration updates tied to change-of-address notices take effect right away, instead of waiting 30 days. The changes apply only to change-of-address notices sent on or after the law’s effective date.

TX-2025892-SB8.s: Texas SB 8 would require certain state and local buildings to set shared restrooms, locker rooms, changing rooms, and showers for use by one sex only, with some exceptions for care, repairs, emergencies, young children, and similar needs. It would also require inmates to be housed by sex and limit some female-only family violence shelters to female victims and their children. If a state or local body violates the law, it could face fines, and affected people or the attorney general could sue to enforce it.

TX-2025892-SR12.s: The Texas Senate adopted a memorial resolution honoring George Wayne Hines of Sulphur Springs, who died on March 7, 2025, at age 85. It offers sympathy to his family and asks that an official copy be prepared for them.

TX-2025892-SR13.s: The Texas Senate resolution honors the life of Mary E. Larsen Preuss Wilson of Sulphur Springs and offers condolences to her family. It says she died on June 23, 2025, at age 92, and includes an official copy for her family. The Senate also agreed to adjourn that day in her memory.

TX-2025892-SR14.s: The Texas Senate adopted a memorial resolution honoring David Max Fowler of Sulphur Springs. It pays tribute to his life, offers condolences to his family, and asks for an official copy to be prepared for them. The Senate also adjourned that day in his memory.

TX-2025892-SR16.s: The Texas Senate adopted a memorial resolution honoring the life of Phillis Hastings Townes of Detroit, who died on March 8, 2025. TX-2025892-SR18.s: The Texas Senate resolution pays tribute to Harry James Sims of Sulphur Springs, who died on March 12, 2025. The committee would have five senators, appointed by the Senate president, and it would review what happened around July 4, 2025. It would operate under Senate rules and state law for such committees.

TX-2025892-SR27.s: The Texas Senate resolution pays tribute to Kenneth Edward Gray of Hooks and offers condolences to his family and friends. It also calls for an official copy to be prepared for his family and says the Senate adjourned that day in his memory.

TX-2025892-SR29.s: This Senate resolution honors the life of Dee Lou Massey of Pickton, who died on June 1, 2025. It extends condolences to her family and asks that an official copy be prepared for them. The Texas Senate also adjourned that day in her memory.

TX-2025892-SR31.s: The Texas Senate resolution honors the memory of Charles Glen Patton of New Boston and offers condolences to his family. TX-2025892-SR32.s: The Texas Senate resolution commemorates the 2025 Wild West Festival BBQ Cook-Off in Springtown on September 20, 2025. TX-2025892-SR41.s: The Senate adopted a resolution commending Denisse Vargas for her service as a legislative intern in State Senator Brent Hagenbuch’s office. TX-2025892-SR43.s: The Texas Senate resolution would recognize Ciclaly Elizarraras for her service as a legislative intern in State Senator Brent Hagenbuch’s office during the summer of 2025 and the 1st Called Session of the 89th Texas Legislature. TX-2025892-SR48.s: The Texas Senate resolution recognizes Alicia Thomas for her service as city secretary of DeSoto and notes her work with city records, elections, and record-keeping. It also says a copy of the resolution would be prepared for her as a sign of respect from the Senate.

TX-2025892-SR54.s: The Texas Senate resolution recognizes Children's Emergency Relief International on its ribbon-cutting and the dedication of the George M. Cowden Building as its new Austin headquarters. It says the nonprofit helps orphans, vulnerable children, and families in crisis in several countries, and that the new building will house its main work and may also be used by other Austin nonprofit groups. The resolution also honors George M. Cowden and sends best wishes for the ceremony.

TX-2025892-SR55.s: The Texas Senate adopted a resolution honoring Antone's Nightclub on its 50th anniversary. It recognizes the club's long role in Austin's blues and live music scene and its place in the city's music history. A copy of the resolution would be sent to the club as a sign of respect from the Senate.

TX-2025892-SR57.s: The Senate resolution would honor Richard L. Jankovsky III on his retirement after 23 years with the Texas Department of Public Safety. It also notes his service in the U.S. Coast Guard and his work in disaster response and border security. A copy of the resolution would be sent to him as a sign of respect.

TX-2025892-SR58.s: The Senate adopted a resolution recognizing the members of the Washington's Birthday Celebration Association and its president for planning the annual Washington's birthday celebration in Laredo. It also notes that the celebration pays tribute to George Washington and that the 128th celebration will run from January 15 through February 28, 2026. A copy of the resolution would be prepared for the group as a sign of esteem from the Texas Senate.

TX-2025892-SR6.s: The Texas Senate resolution honors and remembers Lamar Gene Urbanovsky, a former Texas State University System chancellor, and extends condolences to his family. It also asks that a copy be sent to his family and that the Senate adjourn in his memory.

TX-2025892-SR60.s: The Texas Senate resolution pays tribute to Virginia Lee Cude of Gilmer, who died on July 19, 2025, at age 81. It offers condolences to her family and asks for an official copy to be given to them. The Senate also adjourned that day in her memory.

TX-2025892-SR61.s: The Texas Senate resolution pays tribute to Jimmie Ruth Jaynes Ford of Jefferson after her death and offers condolences to her family and friends. It also asks for an official copy to be prepared for her family. The Senate adjourned that day in her memory.

TX-2025892-SR62.s: The Texas Senate adopted a resolution to congratulate Bill Presson of Longview for receiving the Korean Ambassador for Peace Medal from the Republic of Korea. It notes that the medal is given to U.S. veterans of the Korean War and says an official copy of the resolution would be prepared for him. The resolution also recognizes his military service during the Korean War.

TX-2025892-SR63.s: A Texas Senate resolution honors the memory of Barbara Wilkison Bell of Longview and extends condolences to her family and friends.

TX-2025892-SR66.s: The Texas Senate adopted a memorial resolution honoring the life of William Bernard “Bill” Collins Jr. of Gilmer. It also offered sympathy to his family and asked for an official copy to be prepared for them.

TX-2025892-SR70.s: This Senate resolution honors the memory of Maxey Wayne Bruner of Longview, who died on July 12, 2025, at age 90. It notes his Navy service, long career at Texas Eastman, faith, and family, and extends condolences to his relatives and friends. The Texas Senate adopted the resolution on September 4, 2025.

TX-2025892-SR71.s: The Texas Senate resolution honors the life of Debra Rene Clouatre of Gladewater and offers condolences to her family and friends. It also directs that an official copy be prepared for her family and says the Senate adjourned in her memory.

TX-2025892-SR73.s: The Texas Senate resolution recognizes John Ross Campbell for 50 years of service with H-E-B Grocery Company in Laredo. It also notes his work in genealogy and says a copy of the resolution would be prepared for him as a sign of esteem from the Senate.

TX-2025892-SR74.s: The Texas Senate adopted a resolution honoring Judson Whitley on his Wish Reveal Celebration. It recognizes his wish to swim with dolphins in Hawaii and notes the help of Make-A-Wish Texas Gulf Coast and Louisiana and Caldwell Companies in making it happen. A copy of the resolution would be given to Judson and his family as a keepsake.

TX-2025892-SR77.s: The resolution honors Leia's Kids on the occasion of its first gala in Frisco on September 4, 2025. Leia's Kids is a nonprofit that helps children and young adults facing pediatric cancer by giving financial grants, hosting dream parties and retreats, and raising awareness. It also sends the group best wishes for a meaningful event and calls for an official copy to be given to the organization.

TX-2025892-SR79.s: The Texas Senate resolution would recognize New Hope Baptist Church in Big Sandy on its 170th anniversary. It would also ask that an official copy be prepared for the church.

TX-2025892-SR80.s: The resolution pays tribute to H. A. "Jack" Jones Jr. of Mineola and extends condolences to his family and friends. It also asks that an official copy be prepared for his family. The Texas Senate adopted it on September 4, 2025.

TX-2025892-SR84.s: The Texas Senate adopted a resolution congratulating James T. Worthen on his retirement as chief justice of the Twelfth Court of Appeals in Tyler. It notes his 27 years as a judge, including service on the court since 1999 and as chief justice since 2003. The resolution also says an official copy will be prepared for him as a sign of respect from the Senate.

TX-2025892-SR9.s: The Texas Senate adopted a resolution honoring Dr. Betty J. Reynard for her work in higher education and her long service as president of Lamar State College--Port Arthur. It recognizes her career, her leadership at the school since 2014, and her many awards and roles in education groups. The resolution also sends her best wishes for the future.
